subject: covariances between exogenous variables if the model includes categorical data, sem

messages.author: 800d5e19995b41e2
messages.subject: covariances between exogenous variables if the model includes categorical data, sem
parts:
Hi,

I have the following cross-lagged panel model:
model <-'
tr2 ~ tr1 + in1
tr3 ~ tr2 + in2
in2 ~ tr1 + in1
in3 ~ tr2 + in2
tr2 ~~ in2
tr3 ~~ in3'
fit <- sem(model, data = forR.spss, ordered=c("tr2", "tr3"), missing="pairwise")
summary(fit, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)

The variables tr1, tr2, tr3 are dicothomies, the variables in1, in2 and in3 are continuous. The problem is that I need to estimate the covariance between tr1 and in1 (tr1 ~~ in1). If I include this, the error mesage appears saying that  "model syntax contains variance/covariance/intercept formulas involving (an) exogenous variable(s)". I was trying to add fixed.x = FALSE, but this option is not supported for DWLS estimator.
Do you have any advice how to solve this? Thanks a lot.

Olga

messages.subject: Re: covariances between exogenous variables if the model includes categorical data, sem
parts:
Hi

Is there a reason that you cannot use the observed covariance between tr1 and in1 as the estimate?

Mikko

messages.author: 671b14edc9322fa7
messages.subject: Re: covariances between exogenous variables if the model includes categorical data, sem
parts:
Hi

You do not need to adjust your syntax. The covariances are already available in the Psi matrix, when you inspect the coefficient matrices

inspect(fit,"coef")

Mikko

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: covariances between exogenous variables if the model includes categorical data, sem
parts:
On 09/17/2014 10:55 AM, Olga Stavrova wrote:
> I just tried this out - it only prints the th coefficients for tr2, tr3,
> in2 and in3 (tr1 and in1 are not included in the matrix).

In the categorical setting, the variances/covariances of exogenous
variables (in your case, tr1 and in1) are NOT model parameters. We just
use the observed variances/covariances:

inspect(fit, "sampstat")$cov

Yves.
